MUQATIL:18:103-107/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:103-107/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:103-107/r2.claim: Their effort is wasted, yet they think they are doing good.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r1.claim: Al-Suddī says the people's effort goes astray, though they think they are doing well; Yaḥyā identifies them as the People of the Book.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r2.speaker: علي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p210/r2.claim: When Ibn al-Kawwāʾ asked ʿAlī who the verse describes, ʿAlī answered: the people of Ḥarūrāʾ.

ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r2.claim: The people meant are disbelievers whose works do not benefit them; another verse says God frustrates the deeds of disbelievers.

ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p314/r3.claim: الذين may be genitive as an adjective for الأخسرين or nominative as a new sentence; يحسبون has two readings.

NAHHAS:v2p475/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p475/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p475/r8.claim: ‘Those whose effort was lost’ can modify ‘the greatest losers’ in the genitive, or be a nominative meaning ‘they,’ or an accusative meaning ‘I mean.’

SULAMI:v1p418#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p418#2/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
SULAMI:v1p418#2/r1.claim: People ruin their good works by reproaching recipients and demanding thanks, and ruin worship by performing it for show and reputation.

THALABI:v6p200#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p200#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p200#2/r4.claim: They are people whose worldly effort went astray while they thought they were obedient and doing good.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r1.claim: “Those whose striving went astray” can be genitive as an adjective of “the greatest losers,” or nominative as a fresh sentence meaning “they are those.”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r2.claim: Their effort and work in worldly life were fruitless, though they believed they were doing well.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p165/r3.claim: “Sunʿ” is the verbal noun of doing a favor and is most often used for good works.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:100-104/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:100-104/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:100-104/r5.claim: Their effort is void in worldly life even though they imagine their deeds are obedient and virtuous.

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r1.claim: Hisban and zann are near synonyms; liqaʾ means nearness without separation, and meeting and contact are related terms; mockery and derision are synonyms.

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r13.claim: Those who assume worship of others benefits them are the greatest losers: they exhaust themselves in deeds they think right, then end in the Fire.

JISHUMI:v6p4503/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4503/r14.claim: One sense of their lost effort is that they tried to destroy religion but failed to attain their aim.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وسعد بن أبي وقاص
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r2.claim: They identify the losers as Jews and Christians.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r3.claim: Another view identifies them as monks who confined themselves to monasteries.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r4.claim: He identifies them as the people of Ḥarūrāʾ.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p210#2/r5.claim: Their effort was null and void in worldly life, although they thought their work was good.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p544#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p544#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p544#3/r6.claim: The question about the greatest losers is a taunting rebuke addressed to the disbelievers.

TABRISI:18:99-105/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:99-105/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:99-105/r7.claim: The greatest losers in works are disbelieving Jews and Christians whose efforts in worldly life came to nothing while they thought their actions were virtuous acts of obedience and worship.

TABRISI:18:99-105/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:99-105/r8.speaker: العياشي
TABRISI:18:99-105/r8.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits that Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali about the greatest losers: Ali identified scriptural communities who disbelieved and innovated, adding that the Khawarij were not far from them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#3/r1.claim: Their effort and work in worldly life came to nothing even while they believed they were doing good.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p197#3/r2.claim: Their leaders know what is correct but choose falsehood to preserve their status; their followers imitate them without evidence.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:99-105/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies them as the disbelievers of Mecca.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:104/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:104/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:104/r1.claim: Their efforts are wasted through disbelief and self-admiration, like monks who lose both worldly life and the next; the clause can be parsed as predicate, apposition, or blame.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:104/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:104/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:104/r2.claim: They imagine their work is good because of vanity and conviction that they are right.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p28#5/r1.claim: Their effort was wasted and void; the relative clause is nominative, meaning “they are those” whose effort went astray.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r5.claim: Ḍalla saʿyuhum means their effort perished, became void, and vanished. Yaḥsabūn and yuḥsinūn differ only by dots, an example of tajnīs al-taṣḥīf.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r6.speaker: البحتري، شاعر مجهول
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p230/r6.claim: Al-Buhturi's line illustrates the dot-based wordplay; another poem is given in a deliberately mispointed form, then restored as “you watered me, my Lord …,” for the same unusual pun.

SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r1.claim: الذين ضل may be genitive as adjective, appositive, or explanatory substitute; accusative for censure; or nominative as predicate of an omitted topic.

SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r2.claim: The closeness of يحسبون and يحسنون is a strong example of orthographic wordplay, called تجنيس التصحيف or تجنيس الخط.

SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r3.speaker: البحتري
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r3.claim: Al-Buhturi's verse contrasts المغتر بالله from غرور with المعتز بالله from عز, illustrating the wordplay.

SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r4.speaker: شاعر مجهول
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r4.claim: A cited poem's wording is then deliberately misread into a different sequence of near-identical written words to show the device.

SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r5.speaker: رسائل الفصحاء
SAMIN-DURR:18:104/r5.claim: An eloquent-letter example strings together similar written forms in قبل قبل يدك ثراك and عبد عند رخاك رجاك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r1.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r1.claim: Asked whether the greatest losers are the Haruriyya, Sa'd answers that they are Jews and Christians: Jews rejected Muhammad, while Christians denied food and drink in Paradise; the Haruriyya break God's covenant after pledging it, and Sa'd called them profligates. Bukhari transmits this.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب والضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r2.claim: Ali, al-Dahhak, and others identify the greatest losers as the Haruriyya.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r3.claim: The verse broadly includes the Haruriyya alongside Jews, Christians, and others; it is not exclusive to any group, since it is Meccan, before the relevant Jewish-Christian address and before the Khawarij existed. It covers anyone who follows an unapproved way while thinking the work is accepted, as echoed in 88:2–4, 25:23, and 24:39.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p201#2/r4.claim: The greatest losers are those whose efforts were invalid under a lawful, pleasing religious way, yet who believe they are doing well and that their deeds are accepted and loved.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r3.claim: Their effort went astray because they turned from the only one who can benefit or harm them toward things that do neither.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p509/r4.claim: Despite the obvious failure, they imagine their work is expertly done because their judgment is weak.

DURR-FULL:v5p465/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r5.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r5.claim: Ka'b says the Quran appears as a beautiful, fragrant companion to the person who acted by it, soothes his terror, and identifies itself as his good deeds.

DURR-FULL:v5p465/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r6.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v5p465/r6.claim: The Quran asks God to intercede for its companion, reminding Him that it occupied his days with thirst and nights with wakefulness; he is then crowned and robed in honor.

BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r3.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r3.claim: Al-Irshad reads this as unbelievers whose deeds were good in themselves, such as charity and freeing slaves, and who proudly expected reward from them.

BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r4.claim: Their efforts to establish intrinsically good works are entirely wasted; the loss of their effort is not limited to worldly life.

BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r5.claim: They imagine their efforts will benefit them in the afterlife because they admire the works they struggled to perform and think they did them properly.

BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r6.claim: The inward warning includes innovators, people seeking reputation, and the ostentatious: even slight ostentation is hidden shirk that cancels deeds.

BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p233#3/r7.claim: Deeds alongside disbelief or hidden association are rejected; this also warns against people seeking thanks from others and monks who impose harsh retreats while imagining they worship rightly.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r1.claim: Their effort is wholly lost and void before God; “in worldly life” modifies their striving, since its failure is not limited to this world.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r10.claim: Doing a deed حسنًا means performing it suitably; they believe they work properly because they admire and invested effort in their acts.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r11.claim: The circumstantial clause may modify the subject of “went astray” or their “striving”; the first makes their misguidance coincide with their mistaken belief and better exposes their error.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r12.claim: The similar forms يحسبون and يحسنون produce a pun-like transposition of letters.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r13.speaker: البحتري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r13.claim: Al-Buhturi’s line about the one who trusts in God and the one who seeks Him illustrates the sound-play.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وسعد بن أبي وقاص ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r2.claim: One transmitted interpretation identifies the people as Jews and Christians; their deeds include acts of worship whose rules were abrogated.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r3.claim: Other identifications are monks who impose harsh ascetic exercises on themselves, and the Sabians.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r4.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r4.claim: When Ibn al-Kawwa asked about them, ʿAli reportedly said they were the Haruriyya, the Kharijites.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r5.claim: An objection says the next verse calls them unbelievers, unlike Kharijites who do not deny resurrection; the answer is that مِن can mean sharing only their misguidance, or ʿAli may have judged them unbelievers.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r6.claim: The author favors reading ʿAli’s attribution as a harsh allusion rather than a precise identification of the verse’s subjects.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r7.speaker: العياشي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r7.claim: A report cited by al-ʿAyyashi says ʿAli identified them as People of the Book who disbelieved in God and innovated in religion; it adds that the river people are not far from them.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r8.claim: This report supports the earlier reconciliation and indicates that the description extends broadly to unbelievers.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p47#3/r9.claim: The relative clause may answer an implied “who are they?”, explain الأخسرين, describe or substitute for it, or be an accusative rebuke; the last analysis fits poorly because its opening does not state the key loss.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p45/r1.claim: The passage answers those who worship useless idols as patrons and seek their favor, making their work and effort futile; the key rebuke is that they think they do well.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r1.claim: Those whose effort went astray is an appositive to the losers, extending the description to heighten suspense about their identity.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r2.claim: Ḍalāl means missing the path; unfruitful effort is likened to travel along a road that leads nowhere.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r3.claim: Saʿy literally means vigorous walking and is metaphorical for work, as in 17:19; they worshiped idols believing their acts would fulfill their aims and count as good.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r4.claim: Attributing error to the effort is a figurative attribution: the people themselves went astray in their efforts.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p46/r5.claim: Yaḥsabūn and yuḥsinūn form a paronomasia distinguished by dot placement, an example in the rhetoric manuals.

TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r1.claim: These six verses draw a conclusion from the sūrah’s account of worldly seduction, reliance on protectors besides God, spiritual blindness, and bad outcomes, and prepare for the closing declaration at 18:110.

TABATABAI:18:103-105/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r3.claim: A person may lose in an undertaking because the effort misses its goal, like a mistaken journey or lost capital; such a loss may be repaired if its cause is recognized.

TABATABAI:18:103-105/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r4.claim: The worst loss is to suffer while believing one profits: unlike an acknowledged mistake, it offers no hope of correction because the person does not see the failure.

TABATABAI:18:103-105/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:103-105/r5.claim: Those who settle in falsehood and mistake it for good are the most hopelessly lost: worldly desires, arrogance, and inherited zeal veil the truth and block its call.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: These verses humble people who thought themselves superior and mocked revelation: they will become insignificant and taste Hell as the consequence.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r1.claim: People direct their efforts toward their aims: seeking God’s pleasure and the afterlife leads to one kind of work, while pursuit of worldly gain leads to another.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:103/r2.claim: Polytheists think their idols bring them nearer to God and that shirk is obedience, but God gives their deeds no value in this life or the next.

QIRAAT-ER:18:104:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:104:9#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:104:9#1/r1.claim: Kasra on sīn is a canonical dialectal variant; grammarians associate yaḥsabu with Hijazi and yaḥsibu with Tamimi.

STUDYQURAN:18:103/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:103/r2.claim: They consider their work virtuous, as other verses say the deeds of disbelievers and wrongdoers seem fair to them.
